fixes.explanation: Moses and the elders don't show up in this psalm, friend. It names the target right in verse 2: the kings gather "…against the LORD and against His Anointed One…" So the opponent here is much higher up than any group of elders.
You got it, baker. The kings say, "Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords." Breaking them and casting them away is exactly what they say they want.
That's the opposite of what they say, friend. The kings say, "Let us break Their chains and cast away Their cords." Breaking and casting away is what they say, not gathering and holding tight.

Nope, hiding isn't in the verse, friend. The psalm says, "The One enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord taunts them." Then He rebukes them in His anger and terrifies them in His fury, which is verse 5.
Right, baker. After the laugh comes a rebuke: "Then He rebukes them in His anger, and terrifies them in His fury…" Then He says, "I have installed My King on Zion…" So the laugh isn't the last word.
That's it, baker. He says, "I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain." Notice the word "have." God announces it as something He has already done.
A flood is a real thing in the Bible (Genesis 7:17), but it isn't in this psalm. Here, God announces, "I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain." No water here, just a King installed.

Fire coming down from heaven is a real thing in the Bible (1 Kings 18:38), but it isn't in this psalm, friend. Here the announcement is, "I have installed My King on Zion, upon My holy mountain." He talks about a King He has installed.

The psalm says nothing about a short time, friend. What it does say is that the nations become His inheritance, and "…the ends of the earth Your possession." That's about what He's given, and the psalm doesn't put a time limit on it.
Egypt never comes up in this psalm, friend. The kings are told, "Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling." That's what the verse tells them to do.
Money never comes up in this psalm, friend. The kings are warned they could "…perish in your rebellion…" Rebellion is the word the psalm uses, not poverty.
Careful, friend, the psalm says the opposite. It says "…when His wrath ignites in an instant." Nothing slow about that. Instant is the word, not slow.
